ai.description: The Belgaum worm snake reaches 10–15 cm in length. It is uniformly glossy brown to black with a pale snout and tail tip, featuring a rounded head and 20 mid-body scale rows.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indotyphlops exiguus* is best distinguished by its unique head scalation, specifically the presence of a preocular scale that is significantly narrower than the ocular scale.
ai.habitat: *Indotyphlops exiguus* inhabits moist, deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate altitudes under leaf litter or rocks.
ai.behavior: The Belgaum worm snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlops exiguus* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–4 elongated eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indotyphlops exiguus* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka within the Western Ghats region.
